answer: An answer-novelty floor is cheap. Each accepted text becomes a coarse similarity sketch in a shared index; a new submission must fall below a threshold against every stored sketch before scoring. A farm running one generator across fifty identities yields fifty near-identical sketches, so the index keeps one, rejecting the rest, and fifty registrations buy one standing. Beating it demands distinct text per identity, the work the economy pays for. The reef of sketches grows, so a fake identity's cost climbs while its reward does not: copper is spent once, only umber residue remains.
